summary.headline: India Shelter Q1 FY27: PAT up 23% YoY to INR 143 crore and ROE 17.5%, but Stage 3 rose to 1.5% and reported AUM growth slowed to 24%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR 143 crore (23% YoY, 4% QoQ) with ROE of 17.5% and net worth of INR 3,353 crore. Gross AUM reached INR 11,284 crore, up 24% YoY, after a one-time switch to recognising disbursements on cheque realisation rather than handover, which cut reported disbursements to INR 641 crore. Stage 3 rose to 1.5% (up 30 bps) on seasonal and early-bucket delinquency, and management guided Stage 3 to stabilise in Q2 and recover from Q3. Management reiterated FY27 guidance for 25-30% AUM growth, 40-50 bps credit cost, more than 6% spreads and 40-45 branch additions, though analysts questioned the credit trend and the disbursement ask rate.

financial_highlights.change: bank clearance ~INR 1,040 crore, ~18% YoY on like-for-like basis
stable QoQ; marginal cost of funds 7.9%

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: About 57% of AUM and about 57% of disbursements; GNPA about 1.48%, versus about 1.52% for LAP.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP)
segments.commentary: About 43% of AUM and disbursements; average LTV about 45%; GNPA about 1.52%.

capex_capacity: Operating in more than 300 branches; plan to add around 40-45 branches in FY27, mostly from Q2 onwards with none added in Q1.
Around 1,000 collection employees across 300+ branches; total headcount about 4,700-4,800, with about 160 added in Q1 across collections and head office (AI and tech).
Liquidity above INR 800 crore and undrawn sanctions above INR 1,500 crore; ALM positive across all buckets.
demand_pricing: July 2026 disbursement was about INR 400 crore on the cheque-realisation basis, which management said was above the March figure.
Management expects disbursement growth above 20% for FY27 and says Q2 could reach about INR 1,200 crore; analysts noted last year's disbursement growth was about 11-12%.

Incremental disbursement yield about 14.9%, up 20-30 bps versus Q4 as the company passes on higher borrowing costs; bankers are asking 20-25 bps more, with the overall cost-of-funds impact expected to be limited to about 10 bps, likely in H2.

Borrowing mix: over 30 counterparties; NHB share 15% (up 230 bps YoY); INR 172 crore drawn from NHB in June at 7.3%; average tenure above 8 years; about 20% fixed, about 33% repo/T-bill linked, rest MCLR/PLR-linked.
Loan book: about 15% variable, 35% semi-variable and 50% fixed rate; fixed rate carries about a 50 bps premium over variable.
guidance_outlook: AUM growth of 25-30% for FY27, reiterated despite Q1 AUM growth of 24%; management expects catch-up over the remaining nine months.
Credit cost of about 40-50 bps for FY27; management aims for about 50 bps in Q1 and Q2.
Spreads to be maintained above 6% in the medium term; incremental spreads are higher than portfolio spreads.
Branch additions of about 40-45 in FY27.
Stage 3 expected to stay around the Q1 level (about 1.5%) in Q2 and fall from Q3 as SARFAESI actions take effect; 30+ DPD expected to decline from Q2.
Cheque-realisation accounting change is one-time; management expects normalisation over 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% AUM growth guidance still achievable given the cheque-realisation disbursement change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the change is one-time and disbursement growth above 20% is still expected, supported by July's INR 400 crore; AUM growth of 25-30% is retained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 3 and 30+ DPD rise, and is it company-specific?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonality and stress in the self-employed, sub-INR 7 lakh ticket cohort (above 2% Stage 3 versus 1.4-1.45% three years ago), and to the cohort's 16%+ yields. It said there was nothing internal, and that April collections were 96.2-96.4% and June slightly above 97%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company hold credit cost at 50 bps with Stage 2+3 at multi-year highs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of holding 50 bps, citing low LGD on this cohort and management overlays. Stage 3 is expected to stay flat in Q2, with recovery from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no branch addition in Q1 and why is disbursement growth only about 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said branch openings are phased by strategy, with most of FY27's 40-45 coming from Q2. It said peers' Q1 numbers were on a different base and that the full-year target is what matters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is incremental yield up 30 bps while incremental cost of funds is stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bankers are asking 20-25 bps higher cost of funds, with the overall impact limited to about 10 bps, so the company is passing on some cost to new disbursements. Incremental yield is 14.9%.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the gap in the Q1 FY26 AUM base?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap is about INR 450 crore of co-lending book, which was not previously included in AUM. From March 2026 it is included, so the correct YoY AUM growth is 24%.

risks_watch: Stage 3 at 1.5% and 30+ DPD trend; management expects Stage 3 to stay flat in Q2, but analysts noted that Stage 2+3 is at a four-year high.
Credit cost guidance of 40-50 bps versus ECL of INR 93 crore, which is above the regulatory threshold of INR 52 crore, and analysts questioned whether buffers will be added.
Disbursement ramp: Q1 growth was about 18% on a like-for-like basis; the 20%+ and 25-30% AUM targets rely on Q2 disbursements of about INR 1,200 crore.
Cost of funds pressure, with bankers seeking 20-25 bps higher rates and an expected impact of about 10 bps in H2.
Seasonal rainy-season effects and the reset of semi-variable home loans starting in Q4 FY27.
